newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Surgutneftegaz to invest $22 mln in oil port.
newsitem.headline: Surgutneftegaz to invest $22 mln in oil port.

text.p: Russia's Surgutneftegaz plans to invest $22 million this year in building a new oil terminal in Batareynaya Bay in the Gulf of Finland, the company's president said on Thursday.
Construction of the new port, which will be able to handle 15 million tonnes of mazut and petrol each year, should be completed by 2000, Surgutneftegaz President Vladimir Bogdanov told Reuters.

The port, 60 km (40 miles) from St Petersburg, will cost $200 million to build and a 336 km (200 mile) pipeline from the Kirishi oil refinery will cost another $100 million, Bogdanov said at a ceremony to lay a foundation stone for the terminal.
"The construction of the pipeline should start in the middle of 1998," said Anatoly Prokofyev, chief engineer of the St Petersburg branch of Surgutneftegaz.

The new port will allow the Kirishi oil refinery, which is owned by Surgutneftegaz, to increase its export potential significantly. Up to now the company has transported its production by rail to Ventspils and other Baltic ports.
After work to deepen the harbour, the new port will be able to accommodate two 60-70 tonnne tankers at the same time.
Bogdanov said the company will attract financing from Russian banks to supplement its own funds. It will choose construction companies via tender.

"The first tenders will be for deepening the harbour, building railway connections and for electricity supplies. The tender for the port's general contractor will probably be announced in October or November," Bogdanov said.

He said the Russian government's planned tax code, which was passed by parliament in principle on Thursday, could complicate the construction of the port due to clauses on raising excise duties on petrol and diesel.
"By our calculations, if the new tax code is accepted in its current form, then all investment will become pointless. But I think that common sense will prevail," Bogdanov said.
